subject: Request: Exec sign-off for BrightLane conditional price guard (3yr)
messages:
From: Margaret Lewis <margaret.lewis@brightlane.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.example
Date: 2028-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BrightLane ask: 3yr conditional price guard + renewal protection

Jonas,

Thanks for the conversation this morning. Attached is BrightLane's requested structure for a 3-year commitment: a price lock for 24 months, an uplift cap of 8% year-over-year thereafter, and a renewal protection clause limiting mid-contract repricing for force majeure/tech changes. We need Redwood to commit to these terms to move forward—finance and legal are aligned pending your exec confirmation. See attached: BrightLane_MA_Pricing_Summary.pdf

High level ask:
- Price lock for first 24 months at current list - 12% discount
- Uplift cap 8% YoY after year 2 (floor 3%)
- Renewal protection: for renewal windows, any repricing differences limited to +/- 5% vs prior year unless mutually agreed

Margaret Lewis
Head of Procurement
BrightLane Therapeutics

Margaret — thanks for the detail. Looping in Marissa (AE lead) and Lauren (VP sales) and Kim from finance/legal for a quick exec review. We can escalate to deal desk. I'll summarize economics and propose a conditional approval path.

Key constraints we need to validate for approval:
- Confirm committed minimums (monthly/annual usage) to support discounted TCO
- Define exact renewal window language and what triggers an exception

Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.example
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example
Date: 2028-12-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BrightLane ask: 3yr conditional price guard + renewal protection

Team — adding context from the AE perspective. BrightLane is in the middle of a product launch and the timing is a big reason they are asking for multi-year certainty. Current ask keeps our unit economics but compresses future pricing optionality.

Deal snapshot:
- ARR intent: ~$2.2M first-year run rate after ramp (70% of committed)
- Committed spend (requested): $6.5M over 3 years
- Requested concession vs standard: additional 4% across year 1-2 (beyond our published discount) in exchange for the 3yr commitment and a predictable staging plan

Suggested conditional approval approach for Execs:
1) Approve a 24-month price lock at a 10% effective discount (slightly less than requested) conditional on a signed 3yr MSA and quarterly usage reviews.
2) Accept an uplift cap of 7% YoY after year 2, with a hard floor of 3% to protect Redwood margin.
3) For renewal protection, include explicit carveouts for emerging regulatory changes and major new feature pricing (documented exceptions). Any other repricing requires mutual written agreement.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.docx (proposed wording), pricing worksheet.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas.weber@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: 2028-12-01T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BrightLane ask: legal & finance review notes

Reading through the proposed language. Finance and Legal have the following concerns and redlines: 
- Risk: long-tail exposure if uplift caps are applied to an unexpectedly high usage profile — recommend a committed minimum spend floor and a usage true-up mechanism at the end of each 12-month period.
- Suggested change to uplift wording: cap should be applied to per-unit list price, not percent of invoice, to avoid compounding effects.
- Renewal protection needs a narrow definition: 'material change' should be defined and limited to external regulatory or infrastructure cost changes. Pricing for new products/features should be explicitly excluded unless BrightLane chooses to adopt them.
- Approvals: recommend Exec approval if we accept a discount >10% effective or if we accept a binding 3-year price lock without a break clause tied to minimums.

I've attached a redline of the term sheet (signed_term_sheet_stub.pdf) and a short memo on the usage true-up approach.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Finance (acting)
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas.weber@redwood.example
Date: 2028-12-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BrightLane ask: exec decision path

Team — I reviewed the numbers and the risk memo. Given the strategic value (pilot with top-5 customer in our biotech cohort) and the health of the relationship, I am prepared to grant conditional executive approval under the following limits: 
1) Price lock: approve a 24-month lock but limited to a maximum effective discount of 10% off list.
2) Uplift cap: approve up to 7% YoY after month 24; BrightLane must accept the per-unit cap language suggested by Kim.
3) Renewal protection: approve with explicit carveouts for regulatory/infrastructure cost changes and for opt-in pricing for major new products.
4) Required: signed 3yr MSA, committed minimums (annual spend floor of $1.8M), and quarterly operational review cadence for the first 18 months.

If Legal drafts the MSA language to reflect the above and adds a usage true-up, I will sign. Please route a clean redline and an approval memo through Deal Desk and mark as Exec Approved.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.example

Subject: Final: Exec conditional sign-off for BrightLane (DL-2028-BR-4397)

Margaret — following internal review, Redwood can provide conditional executive approval on the terms below. This approval is contingent on execution of the 3-year MSA with the attached redlines and the commitments listed. Once legal returns a cleanly executed MSA, we'll deliver the final signed term sheet and route a DocuSign envelope for the agreed attachment.

Approved terms (summary):
- 24-month price lock at up to 10% effective discount (as described in redwood_proposal_v3.docx)
- Uplift cap: 7% YoY after month 24, applied to per-unit list price (hard floor 3%)
- Renewal protection: limited carveouts for regulatory/infrastructure changes and opt-in for new products; any other repricing requires mutual written agreement
- Mandatory committed minimum: $1.8M annual spend floor (usage true-up annually)
- Governance: quarterly business reviews for first 18 months; BrightLane agrees to provide monthly usage exports for monitoring

Next steps we need from BrightLane:
1) Execute the attached MSA (redline attached).
2) Confirm DocuSign contact for sign-off and billing details.
3) Confirm acceptance of the annual committed minimum and review cadence.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.docx, signed_term_sheet_stub.pdf

I'll open a Deal Desk ticket and add the approval memo to the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.example/deal/DL-2028-BR-4397.

Jonas Weber
